text:
kai: Heads-up: quick sync to align on KV + prefix cache metrics for Console dashboards, routing policies, and quota/telemetry limits. Proposal below — @tanvi @miguel @sophie please chime in.

tanvi: Primary consumers? Console overview, routing autoscaler, billing/usage team.

miguel: Also runtime ops needs per-GPU hot-key / tenant heatmaps.

sophie: Cardinality is the main risk. Tenant + model + workload explodes. We should hash tenant and bucket workloads.

kai: Proposal metric names (prom-style) and labels:
```
kv_cache_hit_rate{tenant_group,model_family,workload_cat} gauge
kv_cache_evictions_total{tenant_group,model_family} counter
prefix_cache_reuse_per_workload{tenant_group,model_family,workload_cat} gauge
prefix_cache_avg_prefix_len{model_family,seq_bucket} gauge
kv_cache_prefetch_hits{tenant_group,model_family} counter
```
Emit hit_rate as a precomputed gauge (hits/(hits+misses)) to avoid bad aggregations. Add sample_rate label if sampling is active.

alex: Runtime notes:
- We'll compute hit_rate upstream and emit gauge.
- seq_bucket = {"<=64","65-256","256+"}.
- workload_cat comes from a runtime mapping (default: unknown).
- Will attach plan_tier label (free/prod/ent) when available.

miguel: Ingest plan: runtime -> prometheus remote_write -> metrics-store -> Console/Grafana. Contract must spell out label names and types. Aggregation interval = 1m.

tanvi: For routing/quota use cases we need reuse signals at 5m and 1h windows. How do we represent windows? label vs separate metric?

sophie: Prefer separate metrics to avoid extra cardinality. e.g., prefix_cache_reuse_5m and prefix_cache_reuse_1h.

kai: infra action stub created. infra#1423 with starter schema. link: https://go/repo/infra/1423 :thumbsup:

miguel: Ownership proposal:
- eng-platform owns the overview/dashboards and rollouts UX panels.
- eng-runtime owns per-model/per-tenant instrumention code.
- infra owns ingestion + retention.

tanvi: Alerts / SLOs idea: for prod tenants, kv_cache_hit_rate < 0.6 sustained for 10m => warn, 30m => page. We'll refine.

sophie: Eviction counts can be noisy; normalize by traffic, e.g., evictions_per_1k_requests. Runtime can emit normalized metric.

alex: We'll add eviction_rate_normalized = evictions / (requests/1000) to the emit list. Also include a 'seq_bucket' label so we can correlate evictions with seq length.

kai: Decisions so far:
- Metric names above locked pending any objections by EOD tomorrow.
- Use tenant_group = hash_prefix(tenant_id,4) + plan_tier label to reduce cardinality but keep actionability.
- Provide both 5m and 1h reuse metrics as separate series.
- Runtime to emit precomputed hit_rate gauges.

Action items: 
- alex: PR to runtime to emit the new metrics + seq_bucket logic by EOD Fri (owner: alex).
- miguel: Infra ingest proto + Console dashboard skeleton by next Tue.
- tanvi: Define workload_cat taxonomy and plan_tier mapping (owner: tanvi).
- sophie: Propose alert thresholds and normalization formulas (owner: sophie).

miguel: I'll scaffold dashboards with low-cardinality defaults (hash groups, model_family rollups).

tanvi: Telemetry quotas: ensure free orgs don't blow metric ingestion. Need sampling knob at envoy/runtime and a default sample_rate=0.1 for free.

ops-bot: FYI: quota spike yesterday for tenant hash 'a3f1' — temporarily raised sample_rate limit.

kai: Good catch. We'll include a best-practice note in the RFC about sampling settings and quota budgeting.

miguel: One more thought — make labels predictable for Console's metric picker: model_family, tenant_group, plan_tier, workload_cat, seq_bucket.

sophie: Agree. Also add a low-cardinality 'workload_group' fallback for unknown mappings.

kai: OK. If no objections I'll lock names and labels tomorrow and add them to infra#1423 and the RFC. Thanks all.
